channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: UN General Assembly debate Day 4
item.description: Small island leaders at the United Nations General Assembly on 26 September demanded climate justice, stronger ocean protection and increased solidarity. They warned that rising seas are already reshaping national borders and that distant conflicts are producing tangible impacts on their coasts. From the Caribbean to the Pacific, leaders from small island States demanded climate justice, ocean protection and greater solidarity at the UN General Assembly on Friday.

item.title: Poland Offers Financial Incentives To US As Talks On Military Base Advance, Minister Tells RFE/RL
item.description: Poland is offering to pay $15,000 a year for every US soldier stationed on its territory and cover infrastructure costs as Warsaw and Washington move closer to agreeing on establishing a permanent American military base. Poland Offers Financial Incentives To US As Talks On Military Base Advance, Minister Tells RFE/RL.

item.title: Ukrainian Soldiers Brave Russian Drones On Trek To Frontline Settlements
item.description: Ukrainian troops trek nearly 20 kilometers to reach Bilozerske in the embattled Donetsk region. Russian drone and aerial attacks have laid waste to the city that used to house 15,000 inhabitants. Speaking with RFE/RL, one soldier said that "everything is bad" near Dobropillia. Ukrainian Soldiers Brave Russian Drones On Trek To Frontline Settlements.

item.title: Pomp over progress in Xi’s US summit with Trump is a win for China
item.description: While the US president hailed the visit as ‘great’, almost nothing of substance was achieved, which was a win for XiKey takeaways from the Trump-Xi summit in WashingtonIf the Beijing meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in May was the “stalemate summit”, the second round of talks between the presidents of the US and China this week seemed to give up entirely on the idea of breakthroughs.

item.title: Tuvalu urges decisive global action as rising seas threaten its future
item.description: Climate change remains the greatest existential threat to Tuvalu, Prime Minister Feleti Teo told the UN General Assembly on Friday, warning that the pace and scale of international action are still falling far short of what vulnerable island nations need. Tuvalu urges decisive global action as rising seas threaten its future.

item.title: West Bank demolitions accelerate, urgent support for Sudan, Haiti diplacement, AI hub to boost
item.description: The situation in the occupied West Bank continues to deteriorate, the UN human rights office has said, pointing to the “mass destruction” of Palestinian villages and forcible transfer of residents in Msafer Yatta, South Hebron Hills. West Bank demolitions accelerate, urgent support for Sudan, Haiti diplacement, AI hub to boost.

item.title: Nepal PM urges climate justice after ‘Himalayan tsunami’ devastates country
item.description: Prime Minister Balendra Shah addressed the Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah brought a stark warning from the Himalayas to the UN General Assembly on Thursday, saying catastrophic floods that killed at least 1,400 people in his country laid bare the human cost of climate change, and the failure of the international system to protect those least responsible for it. Nepal PM urges climate justice after ‘Himalayan tsunami’ devastates country.

item.title: Six years on from COVID-19, is the world ready for the next pandemic?
item.description: COVID-19 killed millions, shattered health systems and brought the global economy to a virtual standstill. World leaders are meeting Friday to review the lessons learned and cement a new approach to prevention and preparation for the next pandemic. Hopes are high that a World Health Organization-led international agreement can move forward. Six years on from COVID-19, is the world ready for the next pandemic?

item.title: Yemen violence deepens concerns over child hunger crisis
item.description: Aid agencies in Yemen highlighted the growing hunger emergency sparked by renewed fighting between Houthi opposition forces and Government troops, after mobile health clinics reported that hundreds of children displaced by the violence are suffering from the most deadly form of malnutrition. Yemen violence deepens concerns over child hunger crisis.

item.title: Australia urges global cooperation on climate, AI checks and international law
item.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese urged nations to collaborate on climate action, artificial intelligence oversight, and restoring international law at the United Nations General Assembly in New Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese underlined the need for countries to work together to address the climate crisis, emerging technologies such as AI, and the breakdown of international rules, at the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday.

item.title: As Deadline Looms, Ex-US Marine Desperately Seeks Brother At Afghan Refugee Camp In Qatar
item.description: A former US Marine spent days in Doha trying to meet his brother at an Afghan refugee camp that will close on 30 September. The camp houses 2,000 refugees whose planned transfer to the United States was halted by a presidential executive order. The inmates face an uncertain future. A former US Marine has spent days trying to see his brother at a camp in Qatar holding Afghan refugees in limbo after plans to bring them to the United States were blocked by a presidential executive order.

item.title: Deadly New Strikes In Russia's War On Ukraine As Spillover Concerns Mount
item.description: Russia kept up its pattern of relentless attacks on Kyiv, killing a 14-year-old boy and injuring seven other people in a drone strike on an apartment building in the capital on September 25, Ukrainian authorities said. Deadly New Strikes In Russia's War On Ukraine As Spillover Concerns Mount.
